hints.title: Expose the vertex algebraically
hints.body: x2−2bx+c=(x−b)2+c−b2. Thus P has coordinates (b,c−b2). The supplied graph places it to the right of the y-axis.
hints.recap: Completing the square identifies the vertex and its parameter dependence.
hints.pitfall: The graph supplies b>0; do not ignore that sign information.
hints.pause: Write the vertex after replacing b by B.

recall.reminder: Read the vertex from completed-square form.

hints.title: Compare the two horizontal coordinates
hints.body: The new vertex is (B,c−B2). Since B>b, its horizontal coordinate is larger.
hints.recap: Compare the same coordinate in the old and new forms.
hints.pitfall: The coefficient −2B is not the horizontal coordinate of the vertex.
hints.pause: Decide which side of P the new vertex lies on.

recall.reminder: Track how parameters affect a graph landmark.

hints.title: Compare heights using the given sign
hints.body: Use the sign of b from the original graph together with the stated relation between B and b; then compare their squares and the corresponding vertex heights.
hints.recap: Squaring a comparison requires attention to signs.
hints.pitfall: The ordering of two negative numbers would not give the same square ordering.
hints.pause: Determine the vertical movement and match both coordinate changes to a graph.

recall.reminder: Squaring a comparison requires attention to signs.

solution:
The original vertex is (b,c−b2), and the diagram shows b>0. The new vertex is (B,c−B2).

Because B>b>0, it lies strictly right of P and strictly below P. The parabola still opens upwards. Only F has that displacement. Answer F.
